name: Quadrantids
note: A strong but very short peak of medium-speed, often bluish meteors. The radiant in northern Bootes climbs high only after midnight, so the pre-dawn hours are best.

name: Lyrids
note: Fast meteors that sometimes leave glowing trains. Best after about 11 pm once the radiant near Vega is well up.

name: Eta Aquariids
note: Very fast debris from Halley's Comet. From North Dakota the radiant rises only a couple of hours before dawn, so look for long streaks low in the east.

name: Southern Delta Aquariids
note: Mostly faint meteors from a radiant that stays low in the south. Best 1 to 4 am under a moonless sky.

name: Alpha Capricornids
note: Low rates, but slow and famous for bright, colorful fireballs. Visible all night, best around midnight.

name: Perseids
note: The summer favorite: fast, bright meteors that leave trains, from about 11 pm until dawn.

name: Draconids
note: Unusually slow meteors, best in the early evening right after dark when Draco is highest. Usually sparse, but this shower has produced storms.

name: Orionids
note: Fast Halley debris with frequent persistent trains and a broad peak lasting several nights. Best after midnight when Orion is high.

name: Southern Taurids
note: Slow and rich in fireballs. Low rates but visible all night, best around midnight.

name: Northern Taurids
note: Slow fireball producer with a plateau-like peak spanning about ten days in November. Best around midnight.

name: Leonids
note: The fastest shower of the year, with bright trains. The radiant in Leo rises after midnight, so pre-dawn is best.

name: Geminids
note: The year's best shower: bright, often yellow-white meteors. The radiant is up by 9 pm and highest around 2 am.

name: Ursids
note: Medium-speed meteors from a radiant near Kochab in the Little Dipper. Usually modest, occasionally bursts. Best after midnight.
